Nitrate-responsive angina: Rest angina, especially between night and early morning
Marked diurnal variation in exercise tolerance, reduced in morning
Calcium channel blockers (not beta blockers) suppress episodes

Coronary Artery Spasm.Definition: Transient total or subtotal coronary artery occlusion (>90% constriction) with angina and ischemic ECG changes
Coronary Artery Spasm.Triggers: Spontaneous or in response to provocative stimuli (e.g., acetylcholine, ergot, hyperventilation)

Obstructive CAD: >50% lesion by diameter stenosis in epicardial artery
Noncardiac: Exclusion of diffuse or obstructive epicardial coronary disease with normal coronary function
